problem:
Find, in ascending powers of $a,$ the **first three terms** in the binomial expansion of ${(1-2a)}^{9}.$

$(1-2a)^{9}=$
{{field-1}}$\,+\,⋯$
worked_solution:
The first three terms of the binomial expansion for $(1+x)^{n}$ are given by

$$
(1+x)^{n}=1+nx+\frac{n(n-1)}{2!}{x}^{2}+⋯.
$$

By substituting $x=-2a$ and $n=9$ into the above formula, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{(1-2a)}^{9} & =1+9\cdot (-2a)+\frac{9(9-1)}{2!}\cdot (-2a)^{2}+⋯ \\  & =1-18a+\frac{9\cdot 8}{2}\cdot 4{a}^{2}+⋯ \\  & =1-18a+36\cdot 4{a}^{2}+⋯ \\  & =1-18a+144{a}^{2}+⋯\end{aligned}
$$
